name: Multilanga – AI Translation & Multilingual Language Switcher
author: aleksandrgol

sections.description:
AI translation for WordPress that you actually own. Multilanga translates your whole WordPress & WooCommerce site with AI and stores every translation in your own database — not a vendor cloud. Stop paying and your site stays multilingual, forever. It’s the fast, private, no-lock-in alternative to cloud translation services.

Everything runs inside wp-admin — no external dashboard, no separate account — and nothing is sent to our servers until you connect to the AI service.

Features

  • 🌍 Unlimited languages — translate into 35+ languages, with no cap on how many you use, on every plan (including the free one).
  • 🔒 You own the translations — they live in your WordPress database, not our cloud. No lock-in, trivial backups; cancel anytime and your translated site keeps working.
  • 🤖 Automatic AI translation — new content is translated in the background; change a setting or a glossary term and re-translate everything in one click — your manual edits are always kept.
  • 👁️ Visual in-context editor — open a live preview and click any text to translate it in place, with a Page & SEO side panel — or review element-by-element in a clean list.
  • ⚡ Served 100% locally — no external API call per visit, no flicker, and no per-view fees; a viral page costs nothing extra and your cache plugin keeps working.
  • 🔍 Real SEO — dedicated language URLs (/de/, /fr/), automatic hreflang + x-default, translated titles, meta, Open Graph and slugs, localized canonicals, and a per-language XML sitemap.
  • 🛒 WooCommerce ready — products, cart and modern block checkout translate out of the box via the Store API, plus per-language product images.
  • 🎨 Brand-aware AI + glossary — set tone, audience and site context; pin an exact translation or keep brand names untranslated, per language.
  • 🧩 Works with any builder — Elementor, Divi, Gutenberg, shortcodes, widgets and theme strings are all covered, because Multilanga translates the rendered page.
  • 🎚️ Flexible language switcher — a lightweight floating button, the [multilanga_switcher] shortcode, or a menu item, with your colours, flags (rectangular or round) and names.

How it’s different from cloud translators

Cloud translation services keep your translations on their own servers and charge by words, by page views and by the number of languages. Multilanga keeps everything in your own database, serves pages locally, and never meters your traffic — at a flat yearly price with unlimited AI words on paid plans.

External Services

This plugin connects to the Multilanga API (a service by DoubleCoded) to machine-translate your content. The following data is sent:

  • Content for translation: the text segments of your public pages that need translating, plus the source and target language codes. Sent by a background task when new or changed content is found — never during a regular visitor page view.
  • License & site info: your license key, site URL, plugin and WordPress version, and whether WooCommerce is active. Sent only after you connect to the service (create or enter a license key): when you verify your license and once a day as a heartbeat, so your license can be validated and moved between sites you own. Nothing is sent to our servers before you connect.
  • Sign-up (optional): when you start a free license (the “Start translating for free” button, or the field on the settings screen), the email address shown/entered and your site URL are sent to create the license. Nothing is sent until you click.
  • Checkout (optional): when you choose a paid plan, your license key is sent so we can create a secure Stripe checkout session; payment is handled entirely by Stripe.

No visitor personal data is transmitted, and customer data in WooCommerce emails is never sent for translation. Translations are stored locally in your WordPress database.

  • Service provider: Multilanga / DoubleCoded — Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin — you land on the Multilanga dashboard.
  2. In Settings, pick your original language and the languages to translate into. The switcher, language URLs and manual editing work right away.
  3. To have new content machine-translated automatically, connect to the AI translation service — click Start translating for free for a key, or paste an existing one (optional; everything above works without it).
  4. Open your site with a language prefix (e.g. /ru/) or run a full scan. Review and polish under Multilanga → Translations.
sections.faq:
What happens if I cancel my subscription?

Your site stays multilingual. All translations are stored in your WordPress database and keep being served. Only automatic translation of new content stops.

Does it create duplicate posts or pages?

No. Language URLs are virtual — nothing is duplicated in your database, and uninstalling leaves your content untouched.

Which page builders are supported?

All of them. Multilanga works on the rendered HTML of your pages, so it does not depend on how the page was built.

Can I edit translations manually?

Yes — open Multilanga → Translations, pick a page and edit any segment side by side with the original. Manual edits are never overwritten automatically.

0.46.0

  • Renamed the “Original language” setting to “Original content language” and added a check that warns when your content’s script (e.g. Arabic, Cyrillic) doesn’t match the language you selected — the most common reason a translated site looks incomplete.
  • Added a short optional feedback prompt when deactivating the plugin, so we can learn what to improve.

0.45.20

  • Every built-in feature is now fully functional without any key: the Settings and Translations screens, language routing, the switcher and manual editing are always available. Connecting to the AI translation service is optional and only powers automatic machine translation.
  • Hardened the page-map throttle to key on the resolved post/term instead of the request path, so it can never create unbounded transients.

0.45.19

  • The admin-bar “Translate” link now opens the editor in the language you are viewing (click it on the Russian page and it opens Russian, not the first language); on the source page it still opens the first target language.

0.45.18

  • Really fixed the admin-bar “Translate” link on translated pages: it now reverts the translated slug to the original page, so it always opens that page’s editor (0.45.16 stripped only the language prefix).

0.45.17

  • SEO: new /multilanga-sitemap.xml listing every page and its language versions with hreflang alternates (works even when Yoast/Rank Math replace the core sitemap), advertised in robots.txt. hreflang tags now point each language at its translated-slug URL and include the source language.

0.45.16

  • Fixed the admin-bar “Translate” link opening an empty editor (“No elements recorded”) when clicked while viewing a translated page — it now always opens the correct source page.

0.45.15

  • Dashboard clarity: elements left untranslated because the free word limit was reached now show as a distinct “Needs upgrade” segment on the progress bar (with a count), instead of looking like plain “Not translated” — so the dashboard and the per-page list no longer appear to disagree.

0.45.14

  • New: re-apply your settings to content already translated. Adding a glossary rule now re-translates existing text that uses the term, and a new “Re-translate all AI content” button in Settings refreshes everything with your current description, tone and glossary. Manual edits are always kept.
  • Better AI terminology: the translator is told to use the established term in each language and never translate discipline/category names literally, which noticeably improves domain terms.

0.45.13

  • No limit on the number of languages — the switcher, language URLs and stored translations are fully functional for everyone; only the AI translation service itself is metered by a word quota.
  • Nothing is sent to our servers until you connect to the service (get or enter a license key): no activation ping, and the daily heartbeat only runs once a license exists.
  • All database queries now use prepared statements with bound parameters throughout.

0.45.12

  • Hardening pass before review: safer cookie/request handling, a longer scan lock so multi-language crawls don’t overlap, and the background progress poller now stops cleanly instead of retrying forever when translation can’t proceed.

0.45.11

  • Background translation now finishes on its own and the progress bars update live (no refresh), even on hosts where WP-Cron is disabled.
  • Fixed the per-row “Translate with AI” button in the list not responding on some sites.

0.45.10

  • Important fix: a full scan is now strictly additive and never deletes existing translations. A previous version could wrongly drop translated content as “stale” on some hosts.

0.45.9

  • Whole-site translation now progresses reliably even on hosts where WP-Cron is disabled (it advances while you watch the dashboard), and no longer stalls at 0.
  • Fixed pages showing as both “not scanned” and already-scanned (duplicate rows) and the “N pages not scanned” notice never clearing.

0.45.8

  • The whole-site translation progress now updates live (no need to refresh), and the description makes clear it only translates new/missing text — finished pages are not re-translated.

0.45.7

  • Page-builder templates (Elementor library, reusable blocks, header/footer templates, etc.) are no longer listed or auto-translated as pages — only real content is.
